scenes.dialogue: A criminal case does not move straight from an F I R to punishment. Evidence must be presented, tested and considered.
scenes.shown: A criminal case does not move straight from an FIR to punishment. Evidence must be presented, tested and considered.

scenes.dialogue: Let us follow a contested Sessions trial under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, or B N S S.
scenes.shown: Let us follow a contested Sessions trial under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, or BNSS.

scenes.dialogue: In our illustration, Arjun is accused of murder and denies the allegation.
First, separate investigation from trial. Police submit their investigation report under Section One Ninety Three.
scenes.shown: First, separate investigation from trial. Police submit their investigation report under Section 193.

scenes.dialogue: Under Section Two Ten, the Magistrate decides whether to take cognizance.
scenes.shown: Under Section 210, the Magistrate decides whether to take cognizance.

scenes.dialogue: Section Two Thirty requires the papers to be supplied free, within fourteen days from the accused's production or appearance.
scenes.shown: Section 230 requires the papers to be supplied free, within 14 days from the accused's production or appearance.

scenes.dialogue: A case triable exclusively by the Court of Session is committed to that court under Section Two Thirty Two.
scenes.shown: A case triable exclusively by the Court of Session is committed to that court under Section 232.

scenes.dialogue: The Public Prosecutor then opens the case under Section Two Forty Nine, explaining the accusation and the evidence.
scenes.shown: The Public Prosecutor then opens the case under Section 249, explaining the accusation and the evidence.

scenes.dialogue: Next, the Judge considers discharge under Section Two Fifty. The application may be made within sixty days from commitment.
scenes.shown: Next, the Judge considers discharge under Section 250. The application may be made within 60 days from commitment.

scenes.dialogue: If there is insufficient ground for proceeding, the Judge must discharge with reasons.
Otherwise, Section Two Fifty One requires a written charge within sixty days from the first hearing on charge.
scenes.shown: Otherwise, Section 251 requires a written charge within 60 days from the first hearing on charge.

scenes.dialogue: The charge is explained and the plea recorded. A guilty plea may lead to conviction under Section Two Fifty Two.
scenes.shown: The charge is explained and the plea recorded. A guilty plea may lead to conviction under Section 252.

scenes.dialogue: Arjun contests the charge, so the prosecution's evidence must follow.
Sections Two Fifty Three and Two Fifty Four govern prosecution evidence. Witnesses testify, and documents are presented.
scenes.shown: Sections 253 and 254 govern prosecution evidence. Witnesses testify, and documents are presented.

scenes.dialogue: In Arjun's case, an eyewitness describes the incident, a doctor explains the medical findings, and recordings may be produced.
The defence can cross examine: could the witness see clearly, and does the medical evidence support the account?
scenes.shown: The defence can cross-examine: could the witness see clearly, and does the medical evidence support the account?

scenes.dialogue: Remember, an allegation in a charge sheet is not itself proof of guilt.
Section Three Forty Six generally requires day to day hearings while attending witnesses remain to be examined.
scenes.shown: Section 346 generally requires day-to-day hearings while attending witnesses remain to be examined.

scenes.dialogue: After the prosecution witnesses, and before the defence stage, comes a crucial safeguard.
Section Three Fifty One requires the court to put the circumstances appearing against the accused to him, for his explanation.
scenes.shown: Section 351 requires the court to put the circumstances appearing against the accused to him, for his explanation.

scenes.dialogue: If a witness places Arjun at the scene, he must get a fair opportunity to answer. This is not cross examination on oath.
scenes.shown: If a witness places Arjun at the scene, he must get a fair opportunity to answer. This is not cross-examination on oath.

scenes.dialogue: Every incriminating circumstance must be put to him specifically. The Supreme Court treats this safeguard as no formality.
Section Two Fifty Five is a checkpoint. If there is no evidence that the accused committed the offence, the Judge must acquit.
scenes.shown: Section 255 is a checkpoint. If there is no evidence that the accused committed the offence, the Judge must acquit.

scenes.dialogue: Otherwise, Section Two Fifty Six allows defence evidence. Arjun might call a workplace witness, or produce attendance records.
scenes.shown: Otherwise, Section 256 allows defence evidence. Arjun might call a workplace witness, or produce attendance records.

scenes.dialogue: He need not enter the witness box; Section Three Fifty Three lets him testify on his own written request.
scenes.shown: He need not enter the witness box; Section 353 lets him testify on his own written request.

scenes.dialogue: And throughout, the prosecution still carries its burden of proving guilt.
When the evidence is complete, Section Two Fifty Seven provides for final arguments. The prosecutor sums up, and the defence replies.
scenes.shown: When the evidence is complete, Section 257 provides for final arguments. The prosecutor sums up, and the defence replies.

scenes.dialogue: The prosecution connects the evidence to the offence. The defence points out weaknesses, inconsistencies or reasonable doubt.
But a lawyer's argument is not, by itself, proof of a disputed fact.
Under Section Two Fifty Eight, the Sessions Judge must deliver judgment within thirty days of the arguments ending.
scenes.shown: Under Section 258, the Sessions Judge must deliver judgment within 30 days of the arguments ending.

scenes.dialogue: That period can be extended to forty five days, but only with written reasons.
scenes.shown: That period can be extended to 45 days, but only with written reasons.

scenes.dialogue: The court decides whether Arjun's guilt has been proved beyond reasonable doubt, and gives reasons for acquittal or conviction.
These thirty or forty five days start after the arguments. They are not a deadline for the whole case from the F I R.
scenes.shown: These 30 or 45 days start after the arguments. They are not a deadline for the whole case from the FIR.

scenes.dialogue: If Arjun is convicted, Section Two Fifty Eight, sub section Two, requires a hearing on sentence before punishment.
scenes.shown: If Arjun is convicted, Section 258(2) requires a hearing on sentence before punishment.

scenes.dialogue: The court considers the sentencing material and the parties' submissions, then passes the lawful sentence.
Conviction decides guilt; sentencing addresses its legal consequence. Any appeal is a separate process.
Magistrate trials use different provisions. Warrant cases on a police report follow Sections Two Sixty One to Two Sixty Six.
scenes.shown: Magistrate trials use different provisions. Warrant cases on a police report follow Sections 261 to 266.

scenes.dialogue: Complaint warrant cases follow Sections Two Sixty Seven to Two Seventy, with evidence before charge.
scenes.shown: Complaint warrant cases follow Sections 267 to 270, with evidence before charge.

scenes.dialogue: Both conclude under Sections Two Seventy One to Two Seventy Three.
scenes.shown: Both conclude under Sections 271 to 273.

scenes.dialogue: Summons cases follow Sections Two Seventy Four to Two Seventy Eight, without a formal charge.
scenes.shown: Summons cases follow Sections 274 to 278, without a formal charge.

scenes.dialogue: Remember the main route: charge and plea, prosecution evidence, the accused's explanation, any defence evidence, arguments and judgment.
Sentencing follows if there is a conviction. Always check the case type, and each deadline's starting point.
